transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you. Thank you for seeing me. 

Um... well, I guess I came in because I've been having a little trouble at work lately. I'm a cashier, and I try really hard to do a good job, I promise I do. But, um, I keep sort of... getting stuck? Doing these little things that don't really fit the moment. I hope I'm explaining this okay. 

Like, I'll catch myself just tapping the scanner in a pattern, or... or sometimes I just freeze, you know, with my hand hovering right over the open cash drawer while the customer is just standing there waiting. I try to snap out of it, it's just a silly quirk, really, but... well, my manager didn't really understand, and last week it actually got me written up. I was so embarrassed to be a bother to the customers. 

Is... is that the kind of thing you needed to know? I want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
When you do those tapping or freezing behaviors, do you feel like something bad will happen if you don’t do them?

Oh, um... no, no, not at all. It's not like I'm worried a disaster will strike or anything. I don't want you to think I'm, you know, overly anxious or superstitious. I promise I'm not. 

It's really just... my body just sort of pauses on its own, I guess? I don't have any bad feelings or fears when it happens. I'm just sort of... there. It's just a harmless little habit, really, even if it bothers my manager a bit. 

Is... is that okay? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you also ever make sudden repeated movements or sounds, like blinking, throat clearing, or shoulder jerking?

Oh, no, definitely not. I don't do anything like that. No sudden jerking or... or making noises, nothing disruptive like that at all. I try to be very quiet and polite at work, you know? 

I might blink normally, just like anyone else, but I don't have any kind of... tics, or anything that would bother the people around me. I promise I'm very careful about how I present myself to the customers. 

Does that... does that help clear things up? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Before you do the tapping or freezing, do you feel a strong urge that it has to be done 'just right'?

No, I don't think so. I really don't feel any sort of... urge, or pressure to get it perfect. I'm not trying to be a perfectionist or anything, I promise. 

It's really just... it just happens. I'm not thinking about making it 'just right' or following any kind of rule in my head. I'm just trying to do my job the best I can, and sometimes my body just does that little pause or tap. 

I hope that's the right answer. I'm really trying to be helpful and explain it clearly for you. Is that what you were looking for?
Do the tapping or freezing episodes feel completely involuntary, like something your body does on its own without you choosing to do it?

Um... yes, I suppose that's a good way to put it. It really does feel like I just get stuck. I definitely don't choose to do it, I promise. 

It's just... well, when I'm at the register, I just keep getting stuck doing these things that really don't fit the moment. Like, I'll start tapping the scanner in a little pattern, or... or I'll just freeze completely with my hand hovering right over the cash drawer, right while the customer is standing there waiting for their change. I feel so terrible when they have to wait on me. 

It's... um, well, to be completely honest with you, and I'm a little embarrassed to even admit this, but... it actually got me written up by my manager last week. That's actually why I came in to see you. I really don't want you to think I'm a bad worker, I always try so hard to do a good job. 

Does... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm giving you the right details.
Right before one of these tapping or freezing episodes, do you feel a physical urge or buildup of tension that goes away once it happens?

Um... no, not really. I don't feel any kind of... tightness or tension building up inside me. It's not like a sneeze or an itch that I have to scratch, I promise. 

It just... happens, kind of out of nowhere. I don't feel any sort of physical relief afterward, mostly just... well, mostly just embarrassed that I held up the line or made a customer wait. There's no buildup or release at all. 

I really hope I'm explaining this right for you. Does that make sense? I just want to be as accurate as possible so I can get this sorted out and get back to being a reliable employee.
During these tapping or freezing episodes, do you ever lose track of what's happening around you or have a blank spell?

No, no, I don't lose track of things. I'm definitely still... still there, you know? I don't have blank spells or anything like that, I promise. 

I know exactly what's happening around me. I can see the customer, I can see the register... I just can't always move my hand right then. But my mind is completely clear, I'm not spacing out or forgetting where I am. I'm very focused on my job, even when my body isn't cooperating. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too strange. I just want to make sure you know I'm still paying attention to my work. Is that the kind of information you needed?
Do you ever get unwanted, repetitive thoughts or images that keep coming back into your mind?

Um... no, I don't think so. I don't really have anything like that. 

My thoughts are usually pretty normal, I think. I just focus on my work and trying to be polite to the customers, like a good cashier should. I don't have any strange images or... or things repeating in my head that I don't want there. I promise my mind is very clear and focused on doing a good job. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my mind or anything like that. I'm just a regular person trying to do his best. Does... does that sound okay? I hope I'm being helpful.
When you’re at work, do you also have trouble staying focused or finish tasks because your mind wanders?

Oh, no, definitely not. I don't let my mind wander when I'm on the clock. I actually pride myself on being very attentive at the register. It's... well, it's really important to me to do a good job, so I stay right on task until my shift is over. 

I make sure I finish whatever I start, whether it's ringing someone up or restocking the bags. I really try to be a model employee, you know? I wouldn't want my manager or anyone to think I'm slacking off or not paying attention. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just want to reassure you that my work ethic is still very strong, and I'm taking all of this seriously. Does that answer your question okay?
Can you hold back the tapping or freezing for a little while if you try?

Well, um... I try really hard to. I mean, I don't want to make anyone uncomfortable or hold up the line, so I put a lot of effort into just... trying to push past it and act normal. 

But, if I'm being completely honest... I don't think I can really stop it once it starts. It just sort of... happens, even when I'm telling myself to stop and just scan the next item. 

I really hope that doesn't make it sound like I'm not trying my best. I promise I put a lot of effort into being professional and keeping things moving for the customers. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do these episodes happen as sudden, brief movements or sounds that repeat in the same way each time?

Um, no... definitely not sounds. I don't make any sudden noises or... or quick, jerky movements like that. It's really just the tapping or the freezing up that we talked about, but it's not like a sudden spasm or anything. 

I always try to be very quiet and respectful at the store. I would never want to startle a customer by making a sudden noise or moving weirdly. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Am I doing okay so far? I'm really trying to be helpful.
When the tapping happens, is it always the same repeated pattern each time?

Um, well, no... I don't think it's exactly the same pattern every single time. It's more just... a general tapping, you know? Like I'm just touching the register a few times to make sure everything is... aligned. 

I wouldn't say it's some kind of rigid routine or anything weird like that. I just do it a little bit, and it varies, depending on what I'm ringing up or how the bags are sitting. I really try to keep it subtle so nobody thinks I'm doing something strange. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to be sure I'm explaining it right so you don't think I'm... I don't know, too far gone or something. Is it a good thing that it's not always the exact same pattern?
Have these tapping or freezing episodes been happening since you were a child, or did they start later in life?

Oh, no, no, definitely not since I was a child. I was a very, um, normal, well-behaved kid. I wouldn't want you to think I've had these... issues my whole life. 

It's really only been, well, it's been building up for about two years and four months now. It started right around the time my youngest moved away to the Eastern Shore for college. It was just a big adjustment, you know? An empty house and all that. So it's just a recent thing, really, just a little stress reaction, I think. 

I hope that's better, that it hasn't been happening forever? I mean, it means I can get back to normal pretty easily, right? I'm really hoping you think this is just a minor bump in the road. Does that timeline sound okay to you?
Before one of these episodes starts, do you feel an urge or buildup that gets relieved when you do the tapping or freezing?

Um, no, I wouldn't call it an urge. It's not like a... a compulsion or anything like that. I don't feel this big buildup of tension that I have to release. 

It's more just... I'm working, and then I just need a moment, you know? Just a little pause to tap the register or just stand still for a second to collect my thoughts. It doesn't feel like I'm being forced to do it by some kind of internal pressure. 

I'd hate for you to think I have no control over myself or that I'm driven by these weird urges. It's really just a minor habit, I promise. Is it a good sign that I don't have that buildup feeling? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right impression.
If someone nearby makes a movement, do you find yourself automatically copying or echoing it?

Um, no, definitely not. I don't copy what other people are doing at all. I'm not... I wouldn't do something like that. That sounds a bit, well, strange, doesn't it? 

I just... like I said, I came in because I keep getting, um, stuck doing these little things at the register. Things that just don't really fit the moment. Like the tapping on the scanner, or sometimes I just sort of freeze with my hand hovering right over the cash drawer, even when the customer is standing right there waiting for their change. 

I know it sounds a little silly, but it's just a minor thing, really. Though... I guess I should mention, it did get me written up last week at work. Which is why I'm here, just to get it sorted out quickly so my manager knows I'm taking care of it. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to be completely honest with you so we can fix this little hiccup. Does that sound like something we can easily take care of?
When you’re around other people, do these tapping or freezing episodes ever start after you see someone else do a movement, or if someone mentions them to you?

Oh, um, no. No, it's not like I'm... reacting to other people or anything like that. If someone mentions it, I just get a little embarrassed, but it doesn't make me do it more. 

Like I was saying before, it's just that I get, well, stuck doing these little things at the register that don't really fit the moment. Like the tapping the scanner in a little pattern, or just... freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is waiting. It just happens on its own, not because of anyone else. 

I know I already mentioned that, and that it got me written up last week... I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right. I really don't want you to think I'm, like, mimicking people or being weird on purpose. It's just a little stress habit, right? I'm hoping you see it that way too.
Right before the tapping or freezing starts, do you ever feel a buildup of pressure or an urge in your body that goes away after it happens?

Um, no... I think we might have just talked about that a minute ago, actually. But, um, no, there's no buildup or pressure or anything like that. 

It's really not like an urge I have to satisfy. I promise I'm not feeling some weird tension that forces me to do it. It's just... I'm working, and then it just sort of happens. Like a little pause. 

I'm sorry, I hope I'm not frustrating you by giving the same answer. I just want to be sure I'm being clear that I'm not, you know, out of control or anything. It's really just a minor thing. Am I making sense? I'm trying my best to give you what you need.
When you need to, can you intentionally stop the tapping or freezing for a short time?

Um, well... I try to. I really do. If a customer is looking at me funny, I try to just snap out of it. But... it's hard. 

Like I was saying, it just sort of happens. I'll be ringing someone up, and suddenly I'm just... stuck. You know, tapping the scanner in that little pattern, or just completely frozen with my hand hovering over the open cash drawer. Even with the customer standing right there, waiting for their change. 

I know I keep bringing that up, I'm sorry. I just... I really want to make sure you understand it's not something I'm doing on purpose to be difficult. I mean, it got me written up last week, which was so embarrassing. I've always been a good employee, you know? I really don't want my manager to think I'm slacking off or losing my touch. 

I'm sorry, did that answer your question? I feel like I'm talking in circles a bit, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. I really am trying my best to control it when it happens.
Did you ever have similar episodes like this when you were a child?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I was a pretty normal kid, you know? I always tried to be good, do my chores, get good grades. I didn't really have any... weird habits or anything like that back then. 

Honestly, this whole thing at the register is pretty new. It's just a recent little quirk, I guess. I'm sure it's just because I've been working so many shifts lately. Stress can do funny things to a person, right? 

I really hope this doesn't make me seem like I've always had something wrong with me. I've always been very capable and put-together. I just want to make sure you know that I'm usually very reliable. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for.
When one of these episodes happens, are you able to suppress it if you try, even for a short time?

Um, well, I think we might have just touched on that, actually. Um, but to answer your question again, I really do try to stop it when I can. 

Like I was saying before, if a customer is waiting or looking at me, I try my absolute hardest to just push through it and snap out of it. But it's... it's just very difficult. Sometimes I just can't seem to stop the tapping or unfreeze myself right away, even if I'm trying to. 

I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself, I really don't mean to be difficult or confusing. I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly. I promise I'm trying my best to manage it at work. I hope that's okay?
